title: AZ-level PCIe & Memory vs Tensor Throughput (H100/A100/L40S) - Quick Notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick investigative notes exploring how AZ-level PCIe/host-path differences (and driver/CUDA combos) amplify memory-bound vs compute-bound behavior across H100, A100, and L40S SKUs. This is intentionally a working doc — rough traces, hypotheses, and reproducible steps.

High-level takeaway (TL;DR):
- Compute-bound workloads (dense tensor ops, short KV cache hit-rate) scale predictably across SKUs given same driver/CUDA; H100 shows best raw tensor throughput as expected.
- Memory-bound workloads (prefill + long-context KV warmups, host->device DMA heavy) exhibit surprisingly high AZ variance — p99 latency and tail spikes correlate with subtle PCIe root complex noise and host NIC/CPU affinity.
- Certain driver/CUDA combos (driver 545 + CUDA 12.2) reduced NVLINK/card-local variance but amplified host DMA stalls on A100 EC2 SKUs in one AZ.

Why this matters:
- We optimize for tail-latency and cost; memory-bound behavior dominates customer workloads with long contexts and frequent KV spills. AZ-level variability means a global routing policy must account for region+AZ SKU fingerprinting, not just SKU label.

Testbed & Methodology:
- Instances: EC2 p4d.24xlarge (A100), p5.48xlarge (H100), g5dn-moderate-like (L40S-equivalent) — multiple AZs within us-west-2 and eu-west-1.
- Drivers/CUDA tested (matrix):
  - Driver 525 + CUDA 11.8
  - Driver 535 + CUDA 12.0
  - Driver 545 + CUDA 12.2
- Workloads:
  1) Compute-dominated: 8k-decoding loop, batch=1, model=opt-6.7B quantized, KV cache disabled.
  2) Memory-dominated: 8k-prefill + 16k-decode, KV warmups enabled to force host->device DMA and KV spilling.
  3) Mixed: short prefills + recurrent KV lookups simulating chat sessions.
- Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 latency per token, tokens/sec throughput, host CPU steal, PCIe-link error counters, nvml power/clock, ncu sampled SM occupancy, nvidia-smi pcie stats, ethtool stats (for NICs), and top-level perf (context-switches, IRQs).
- Tools & commands:
  - nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,index,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,driver_version --format=csv -l 1
  - ncu --target-processes all --set full --csv --sample 5s -o ncu-run
  - sudo perf record -a -g -e cycles:u,instructions:u -o perf.data sleep 60
  - parse PCIe counters: nvmlTool/pcieStatProbe.py (in repo)
  - host DMA monitoring: iostat -x 1, sar -n DEV 1 60

Configuration matrix (selected):
- SKU / AZ / Driver-CUDA / Workload: ran combinations across 3 AZs each region, 3 drivers, 3 workloads = ~81 runs (short runs, 5–10 iterations each).

Notable observations (raw):
- A100 (p4d) in us-west-2a: memory-dominated runs had p99 per-token latency ~2.1x the same SKU in us-west-2b. CPU-side context switches and host NIC IRQs were 30-50% higher in 2a during DMA bursts.
- H100 (p5) showed lower variance across AZs for compute-dominated runs (<1.1x p99 delta) but memory-bound workloads still had 1.3–1.6x deltas depending on AZ.
- L40S-like instances showed stable decode throughput but lower peak tensor throughput as expected; tail spikes linked to NVMe background GC on some AZs (weird but reproducible when host /var/lib/model-cache on instance local NVMe hit GC).
- Driver 545 + CUDA 12.2 cut down SM-level stalls on H100 (improved IPC by ~8% on compute runs) but coincided with increased host->device DMA latency in one A100 AZ (p99 token latency increased). Hypothesis: newer driver altered DMA batching heuristics or changed interplay with PCIe root complex.

Attribution evidence: what points to PCIe / host path rather than model/router code?
- Correlation between p99 spikes and elevated PCIe replay counters and increased PCIe bandwidth latency (nvml pcie counters).
- perf shows CPU threads pinned to mismatched NUMA node during worst runs; moving serving threads to local NUMA node dropped p99 by ~15% in one test.
- Isolated microbenchmark: continuous host->device memcpy of large pages produced identical tail patterns on the problematic AZ under same kernel/driver, independent of model code.

Representative numbers (approx, average across 5 runs):
- Memory-bound workload p99 per-token latency:
  - A100 us-west-2a: 48ms
  - A100 us-west-2b: 23ms
  - H100 us-west-2a: 29ms
  - L40S eu-west-1b: 36ms
- Compute-bound throughput (tokens/sec): H100 ~1.9x A100 for same model in these tests. L40S ~0.85x A100.

Anomalies / weirdness we hit:
- One AZ had intermittent PCIe replay counter spikes with no hardware alert — vendor support acknowledged hardware-level root-complex resets tied to noisy multi-tenant NIC drivers (they had a workload in same AZ doing heavy SR-IOV).
- NVME GC correlation on L40S-like instances: background ephemeral workload on same host triggered GC; local-step: move model cache to tmpfs fixed it for tests.
- A100 driver-specific host DMA stall: observed only when driver 545 + CUDA 12.2 used together on that AZ; rolling back driver to 535 removed the spike.

Quick reproducible checklist (how to reproduce locally) — run on target AZ and compare with control AZ:
1) Provision identical instance types in two AZs.
2) Install driver & CUDA per matrix.
3) Start baseline compute-run (no KV) and memory-run (prefill with KV warmups).
4) Collect: ncu, nvidia-smi --query, perf, iostat, nvml pcie counters.
5) Run host->device memcpy microbenchmark while collecting PCIe counters.
6) Swap thread NUMA affinity and re-run.

Immediate mitigations suggested:
- When routing requests, avoid AZs that show persistent PCIe/host-path anomalies for memory-heavy routes — introduce AZ fingerprint in routing policy (small dynamic blacklist with time-decay).
- For Dedicated/private customers: recommend driver 535 + CUDA 12.0 as a safe baseline for A100 until vendor confirms root-complex behavior with 545.
- For L40S-based deployments, ensure model cache avoids local NVMe if background GC is observed; use tmpfs or mounted ephemerals with tuned GC windows.

Next investigations (priority):
- Repeat identical tests across other regions (ap-southeast-1, eu-central-1) to see if AZ variance is a global cloud phenomenon.
- Deeper vendor debugging: provide PCIe replay logs + perf traces to cloud provider and driver vendor; ask for firmware/host BIOS checks on flagged hosts.
- Probe NVLINK vs PCIe fallbacks: artificially throttle NVLINK and observe splice to PCIe patterns; quantify performance cliff points where cache spilling crosses NVLINK->PCIe.
- Test with kernel versions (5.10 vs newer) and different CPU governor settings; some evidence that CPU governor/laptop-like power modes increased IRQ latency.

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Is there an easy telemetry signal we can collect in production for quick AZ fingerprinting? PCIe replay counter + host context-switch rate might be a good combined heuristic.
- Could our runtime adapt by increasing small-batch prefetch to hide host DMA jitter? Need eval: tradeoff latency p50 vs p99.

Files & traces location:
- S3: s3://redwood-experiments/az-pcie-memory-2025-02 (raw ncu csvs, perf.data, nvml dumps)
- Small analysis notebook: https://notebooks.internal.redwood/az-pcie-memory-jan25 (in progress)

Conclusion (short):
AZ-level host-path differences materially impact memory-bound inference tails. We should treat AZ as a first-class signal for routing memory-heavy requests, enforce cautious driver baselines for Dedicated, and escalate to vendor/cloud provider with perf traces.

---
End of notes.

(Contains to-do flags: need to 1) reproduce with vendor-supplied telemetry, 2) run longer-duration soak (24h) in flagged AZs, 3) propose routing policy change for next deploy.)
